classification.difficultyReason: Form profit by subtracting cost from revenue, recognise that the downward-opening quadratic is maximised at its vertex, and evaluate the profit there.

content.prompt: The cost of producing $x$ items is $C=2x+50$, and the revenue is $R=-x^2+60x$. Find the number of items that maximises profit, and determine the maximum profit.

answer.short:
29 items; maximum profit $\$791$.

Profit is revenue minus cost; the resulting downward-opening quadratic has its maximum at $x=29$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=R-C\\P(x)&=-x^2+60x-(2x+50)\\P(x)&=-x^2+58x-50.\end{align*}$$
This quadratic opens downwards. Its vertex occurs at
$$\begin{align*}x&=-\frac{58}{2(-1)}\\x&=29.\end{align*}$$
The maximum profit is
$$\begin{align*}P(29)&=-(29)^2+58(29)-50\\P(29)&=791.\end{align*}$$
Producing 29 items gives a maximum profit of $\$791$.
